title: A California house shaped like a flying saucer has hit the market for nearly $1.5 million; built in 1969, the 793-square-foot Futuro home is one of about 50 surviving examples of the space-age design
byline: TOI Real Estate Desk / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Oct 12, 2026, 11:48 IST

content:
A house resembling a flying saucer has been listed for $1.495 million in California’s San Jacinto Mountains, offering a rare opportunity to own a piece of experimental architectural history.

According to SFGATE and The Wall Street Journal, the property, known as the Donaldson Futuro, is located near Idyllwild and is among a small number of surviving homes designed to capture the optimism and futuristic imagination of the Space Age.Built in 1969, the 793-square-foot structure stands out for its bright exterior, circular form and distinctive raised design. Made from reinforced fiberglass-polyester plastic, the home weighs approximately 11,900 pounds and was conceived as a prefabricated dwelling that could be transported to different locations, even by helicopter.

Designed by Finnish architect Matti Suuronen, the Futuro houses were an unconventional response to the era’s interest in new materials, mobility and futuristic living.

A rare survivor of space-age architecture

The Donaldson Futuro is one of roughly 50 to 60 examples believed to remain from the original production of about 100 structures worldwide. Its unusual design has helped it stand apart from conventional residential architecture, while its historical significance has earned it a place on the National Register of Historic Places and recognition as a California historical landmark.

The home’s journey to its current mountain setting was almost as unusual as its appearance. Originally located in San Diego, it was rescued after years of neglect and eventually transported to the Idyllwild area in 2004. Despite the original concept of helicopter-assisted mobility, the relocation required a carefully planned journey by flatbed truck through mountain roads, with the route presenting challenges because of the structure’s size and the limited clearance in some stretches.

The preservation effort behind the home

The property was saved and restored by preservation architect Milford Wayne Donaldson, who had been fascinated by space and futuristic design since childhood. He took on the project after learning that the neglected structure faced an uncertain future, seeing value in preserving an unusual example of mid-century architectural experimentation.Donaldson and his wife, Laurie, later restored the house, taking care to preserve its original character.

The interiors retain their 1960s style, with bright colours, laminate surfaces and shag carpeting. According to architectural preservation organisation Docomomo US, the couple kept several original features, including built-in furniture and Formica laminate countertops. The restoration also required them to meet modern building and safety standards without making major changes to the home's unusual structure.The restoration received recognition from the California Preservation Foundation, while the home’s historic designation further established its importance beyond its novelty as a UFO-shaped residence. It is also noted as the first Futuro house in California approved for residential occupancy.

A new chapter for the Donaldson Futuro

Despite residing near Sacramento, Donaldson and his wife have chosen to continue spending a significant amount of time at their distinctive property.

However, the architect's gradual decline in health has led them to make the difficult decision to put the home up for sale. They hope that the next fortunate owner will not only appreciate the unique architectural and historical significance of this residence but also commit to preserving the extensive efforts that went into restoring it to its current state.With a listing price of $1.495 million, the property stands out as more than just an unusual home on the market. It embodies a historical period in which architects and designers dared to envision homes that could liberate themselves from traditional structural constraints, embracing the vast possibilities offered by modern materials and cutting-edge technology. For its future owner, the Donaldson Futuro presents a remarkable opportunity to take stewardship of a rare artifact of that innovative vision, which has remarkably endured decades of evolving tastes and a challenging journey to achieve its current mountain locale.

Its next chapter will depend on finding an owner who values its history and helps preserve its futuristic legacy for generations to come.
